title: Numeric-format suite: batching & long-window perf characterization for FP8/INT8 serving
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: quantify throughput and tail-latency impact of compact numeric formats (FP8 and INT8) across a realistic serving stack when combined with varying batching policies and long-context workloads. Deliverables: experiment runbook, data artifacts, decision memo recommending default profile families for 1) low-latency interactive routes, 2) high-throughput batch routes, and 3) mixed long-context customers.
experiment_config: Models: Llama-2-13B and Llama-2-70B reference weights (fp32 baseline)
Formats: fp32 baseline, fp8-e4m3, fp8-e5m2, static int8 post-training quant (per-channel), dynamic int8 calibration
Hardware: A100-80GB and H100-80GB pools; single-GPU and 4x-GPU sharded runs
Batching policies: immediate (no aggregation), 32ms adaptive window, 128ms microbatch, fixed batch sizes [1,4,8,16], continuous batching with KV cache coalescing
Context lengths: 512, 2048, 8192, 32768 tokens (long-window), KV cache warm and cold scenarios
Workloads: synthetic single-token p99 latency probes, conversation-style streaming, and throughput-saturated microbenchmarks (steady-state token/s)

Metrics: median latency, p95/p99 tail latency, tokens/s, GPU utilization, peak memory, kernel fallback rate (to fp32/slow kernels), accuracy delta vs fp32 (perplexity and targeted QA prompts), and cost estimate delta
reproduction_steps: Checkout branch eng/bench/num-format-suite and install harness from tools/bench/runner
Provision test clusters using infra/playbooks/bench-a100.yml and bench-h100.yml (tags: perf-suite)
Collect artifacts to s3://redwood-inference-experiments/eng/147305/<run_id> and annotate run with metadata.json
Validate accuracy by running evals/qa-suite against baseline fp32 and compute mean exact-match and perplexity delta
results_summary: High-level: FP8 modes reduce tokens/s cost by ~28-35% vs fp32 at similar median latency for throughput-optimized batching, but show increased p99 tails in long-window cold-KV scenarios

Batching interaction: Adaptive 32ms window combined with fp8-e4m3 gave best tradeoff for 13B single-node: +32% tokens/s, median latency +5ms, p99 +18ms under cold start. Fixed large batches (16) amplify throughput gains but increase median latency for single-token probes

INT8 observations: static per-channel int8 maintained accuracy within 2% perplexity on 13B but required kernel fallback on certain attention patterns for 70B, increasing p99 by up to 120ms on H100 sharded runs
Kernel fallback: fallback incidence correlated with out-of-range activations for long-context (>=8192). fp8-e5m2 showed fewer fallbacks but a slight hit to QA exact-match (~1.5% on average)

Cost proxies: projected per-token GPU cost decreased by ~30% for fp8 modes in steady-state throughput; however, for low-concurrency, latency-sensitive routes fp8 can increase tail-latency cost (customer SLA risk)
Memory: FP8 reduced peak activations memory by ~38% enabling larger effective batch capacity; INT8 had similar memory wins but sometimes required extra calibration buffers
accuracy_validation: Evals run: 10k QA prompts, 5k summarization checks, and perplexity on Wikitext-like holdout
FP8-e4m3 delta vs fp32: perplexity +0.9% (13B), QA EM delta -0.8pp average; within our alert threshold for most product routes
FP8-e5m2 delta: slightly larger perplexity +1.6% but better kernel stability in long-context runs
INT8 static delta: perplexity +1.3% (13B), but 70B showed thin-tail regressions on code synthesis subset leading to targeted review
Decision threshold: mark profiles as green if QA EM delta <=1.0pp and perplexity delta <=1.5% and kernel fallback rate <0.5% for target route
tradeoffs_and_notes: We observed a tradeoff surface between median latency and tail-latency when enabling compact formats under batching aggregation — longer batching windows improve tokens/s but amplify p99 for single-token interactive probes

Kernel fallback is the dominant source of p99 spikes for long-window contexts; mitigations include conservative block quant params, per-layer clipping heuristics, and charging a fallback budget per-route
Calibration workflows for int8 must include long-context representative prompts; short-context calibration underestimates activation distribution tails leading to field regressions
H100 shows fewer fp8 kernel fallbacks than A100 for identical model/format combos; hardware-specific profiling will be required before enabling a profile fleet-wide
Operational: rollout should include canary traffic with automatic rollback when p99 > SLA or QA EM regressions exceed threshold
decisions: Create two default profile families: latency-optimized (fp8-e5m2, conservative batching 32ms max) and throughput-optimized (fp8-e4m3, adaptive batching with cache coalescing)
Enable INT8 static profiles only for 13B-class models after per-customer calibration; block 70B INT8 for now until additional kernel fixes reduce fallback incidence
Add a kernel-fallback metric to Console per-route dashboard and a regression alert if fallback_rate > 0.5% over 10m
Update quant calibration playbook to require representative long-context samples and to run a fallback-sim check
next_steps: Ship runbook and dataset links to SRE and Console teams for dashboard integration (owner: Marco)
Implement automated canary policy: 5% traffic 24h monitoring with QA EM checks and fallback_metric gating (owner: SRE)
Iterate on per-layer clipping heuristics in runtime for fp8 to reduce fallback rate (owner: Runtime team)
Schedule follow-up benchmarking for mixed-concurrency (concurrent small interactive + background high-throughput) by 2026-04-01
